title: Tennis basics
examples: How do you start a point in a game?
What is the difference between a serve and a volley?
Can you explain the scoring system again?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the basics of playing tennis.
First we need to know about the tennis court.
Next we learn how to serve the ball over the net.

draw.text: The serve: hitting the ball over

explain.say: Now let us look at the scoring system in tennis.
A game is won when one player reaches four points.
In real life you see this when playing backyard tennis.

faq.q: How do you score when the score is tied at 40?
faq.a: If the score reaches deuce, you need two more points to win the game. The first point after deuce is called advantage.

faq.q: What is the difference between a serve and a return?
faq.a: The serve is when you start the point by hitting the ball from behind the baseline. A return is hitting the ball back after the serve.
asks: How do I start the point?
What is the first hit of the point?

faq.q: Do I have to serve from a specific spot?
faq.a: Yes, you must stand behind the baseline when you serve the ball over the net. You must also serve into the correct service box.
asks: Where do I stand to serve?
Is there a spot for serving?

faq.q: What is the purpose of the court markings?
faq.a: The markings show where the ball must land for a point to count. Singles and doubles use different areas of the court.
asks: Why are there lines on the ground?
Do I hit it inside the lines?

faq.q: What if I hit the ball out of bounds?
faq.a: If the ball lands outside the marked boundaries, the point is usually lost. This is called a fault.
asks: What is a fault in tennis?
What happens if I miss the court?

facts: A tennis game is won by reaching a certain number of points.
The serve is the action used to start every point.
The court has specific areas for singles and doubles play.

quiz.say: If the score is 15 to 30, and the next point is played, what will the score be?
quiz.why: The score moves from 15 to 30, and then the next point makes it 15 to 40.

wrong.0: This mistake assumes the score resets to equal points after a point is played.
wrong.1: This mistake does not account for the point that has just been played.
wrong.3: This mistake forgets the first player's score and only changes the second player's score.

quiz.say: Which area is used for a singles match?
quiz.why: Singles play uses the entire area marked for one person on each side.

wrong.0: This area is too small to cover the whole court for singles play.
wrong.1: The doubles area is too large and includes space for two players.
wrong.2: The service line only marks where the ball must land, not the whole playing area.

quiz.say: When starting a point, what is the first action?

options.show: Wait for the opponent to hit first
options.say: Wait for the opponent to hit first

quiz.why: Every point must begin with a legal serve from behind the baseline.

wrong.1: Volleying is hitting the ball before it bounces, which is not the start of a point.
wrong.2: You must serve into the correct service box area.
wrong.3: The server must initiate the point with a serve.
